results.title: What is the Metadata Economy? - Scribble Data
results.content: * *Metadata – Make it possible to identify, categorize and search large data sources efficiently*. In this article, we will answer the question “what is metadata?”, understand the principles of data sharing, and explore how these two are related. As another  example, imagine an e-commerce business and a construction company sharing data. Metadata is structured data that helps to reference, sort and identify characteristics of the information it describes. Simply put, metadata is data about data. Good metadata ensures that data has the following attributes:. * **Interoperable:** Metadata allows the integration of different data sets and allows  data to be used with different applications for storage, processing, and analysis. * **Re-usable:** Metadata holds crucial information about the structure of a data set including definitions, information about how data was collected and even guidelines for how it should be read. * **Structural metadata:** Used to  indicate  how disparate elements of a complex data set are related to each other. * **Usage metadata:**  Indicates how data may be used and how it should be controlled. ## What is Data Sharing? A typical data-sharing agreement will include the following items. * **Agreement period**: The agreement  must clearly state when the provider will share data with the recipients, and how long the recipients of the data will maintain access to the data. Guidelines should include language about whether the recipient can share or sell any part of the information or reports they have access to because of the source data. #### How Data Sharing Between Companies Happens in the Real World. To drive home our understanding about data sharing and metadata, let us imagine a situation in which Company A and Company B have entered into a mutually beneficial data-sharing agreement. Once this is in place, data sharing between companies can happen in the following three phases. Detailed metadata aids the TDC in  accurately predicting  which companies can benefit the most from sharing data with each other. + Growing the cycle of trust between companies sharing data. results.title: Creating an NIH Data Management and Sharing Plan – ReproNim
results.content: Creating a Data Management and Sharing Plan An NIH Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP) currently comprises 6 elements covering 1) the type of data and metadata that will be collected and preserved, 2) software tools and code required to use the data, 3) standards used for collecting and organizing data, 4) long term data preservation and access, 5) distribution, reuse, and privacy considerations, and 6) oversight. ReproNim has created a set of CDEs (aka Federated data elements) that provide a standard for the most common neuroimaging packages. The use of ReproNim tools, principles and best practices makes public sharing of data (as well as code and workflows) via OpenNeuro efficient as the data will already be compliant with OpenNeuro requirements.

results.title: Provenance Metadata Standards for Reliable Data
results.content: # Provenance Metadata Standards for Reliable Data ## Data Science Provenance Metadata This article discusses provenance metadata in data science, its applications, standards, and tools. Data provenance metadata describes its origins, modifications, and processes. Provenance metadata makes data history transparent, building trust. By documenting data’s path, changes, and procedures, provenance metadata allows data analysis to be reproduced. Data and model versioning helps capture provenance metadata. Versioning data and tracing its lineage helps capture provenance metadata. **E-commerce:** Tracking consumer and product data with provenance metadata improves trust and personalisation. **Complexity:** Tracking data transformations and procedures to capture provenance metadata is difficult and resource-intensive. Data science provenance metadata’s future consists in addressing difficulties and improving capabilities: Trustworthy and repeatable data science relies on provenance metadata.

results.title: What is Consent Management?
results.content: Consent management is the process and tools used to communicate to users what information you require from them and what will be done with it. Careful consent management means communicating the benefits they receive by sharing their data and the measures you will take to ensure their private information is used responsibly and within regulatory limits. A user's consent in the context of data collection and processing is their explicit permission for you to collect, store, process, and potentially further share their data. Disclosing why the data is collected and detailing how it benefits the user will encourage consent to its use. GDPR, CPRA, LGPD, and other region-specific privacy regulations affect exactly how you must obtain user consent and how the data can be used. Consent management is the process of gaining users’ consent and allowing them to manage the data they’re sharing and the purpose of sharing it. Consent management includes both the policies you adopt for managing user consent and the technical implementation that allows the user to make decisions about how their data is collected or used. Implicit consent is gained on the assumption that the user consents to their data being used in a particular way. Explicit consent is when you tell the user exactly what data you're collecting, where it's being stored, how long it is being stored for, and what you plan to do with it — all in language they will understand. When seeking explicit consent, the user is often given some level of granular control over their data sharing. Your relationship with that user, and the data you will be collecting from them, has changed, and consent must be regained or updated based on the new ways you will be using their data. ### Consent management and first-party data. Consent management platforms such as OneTrust provide the components required to give your users control over what happens to their data. ## Consent management and customer data platforms. However, by using a customer data platform (CDP) that understands consent management and propagates the consent information collected from an integrated consent management platform, this process can be greatly streamlined. In this article we explained consent management, and why it is required when working with customer data.
